simple: Tools are the items players hold and use, like swords, wands, flashlights, and keys. This page shows how to build a `Tool`, where to put it so players get it, and how to make it do something when used. Knowing this lets you add gear to your game, give it as a reward, or sell it in a shop.
analogy: A tool is like a backpack item in real life. It sits in your bag until you take it out (equip), and then you can use it (activate), like switching on a flashlight.
keyPoints: Insert a `Tool` object, then set `TextureId` (its inventory picture) and `ToolTip` (the name shown on hover).
A physical tool needs exactly one part named `Handle`. That is where the character's right hand grabs it.
Weld all parts of a tool together, and do not anchor them, or the player gets stuck when holding it.
Change the tool's `Grip` to fix how it sits in the hand. You usually have to try a few values.
A tool with no 3D model, like a spell, needs `RequiresHandle` turned off.
Put tools in `StarterPack` so everyone starts with them, in `Workspace` so players can pick them up, or in `ReplicatedStorage` to hand them out later by cloning them into a player's `Backpack`.
`Equipped`, `Unequipped`, `Activated`, and `Deactivated` events tell you what the player is doing with the tool.
Tool input happens on the player's device, so most tools need a LocalScript, a server Script, and a RemoteEvent to talk between them.

terms.Handle: The part of a tool that the character's hand holds. It must be named exactly `Handle`.
terms.Grip: A `CFrame` setting that moves and turns the tool compared to the hand holding it. For example, a Grip position of `(0, -1.5, 0)` moves the tool 1.5 studs along the hand's own up/down direction.
terms.CFrame: A value that stores both a position and a rotation together.
terms.relative to: Measured from something else. A tool's Grip is measured from the hand, not from the center of the world.
terms.equip: Take a tool out of the backpack and hold it.
terms.activate: Use the tool, like clicking, tapping, or pressing the right trigger on a controller.
terms.Backpack: A player's inventory. Tools inside it show up in the hotbar at the bottom of the screen.
terms.StarterPack: A container whose tools get copied into every player's Backpack when they spawn.
terms.anchored: A part that is frozen in place and does not move with physics.
terms.WeldConstraint: An invisible glue that holds two parts together so they move as one.
terms.R15 / R6: Two kinds of Roblox character bodies. R15 has 15 body parts and holds tools in `RightHand`. R6 has 6 parts and uses `Right Arm`.
terms.RemoteEvent: A messenger object that lets a LocalScript send a message to a server Script, or the other way around.
terms.clone: Make a copy of an object. `tool:Clone()` makes a new copy you can give to a player.

example.title: Print what the player does with a tool
example.place: LocalScript inside a Tool in StarterPack
example.code:
local tool = script.Parent

tool.Equipped:Connect(function()
	print(tool.Name, "equipped")
end)

tool.Unequipped:Connect(function()
	print(tool.Name, "put away")
end)

tool.Activated:Connect(function()
	-- Runs when the player clicks or taps while holding the tool
	print(tool.Name, "used")
end)

tool.Deactivated:Connect(function()
	print(tool.Name, "released")
end)
explain: The LocalScript lives inside the tool, so `script.Parent` is the tool.
Each event is connected to a function that prints a message in the Output window.
`Activated` fires when the player starts clicking or tapping, and `Deactivated` fires when they let go.
To change the world for everyone, like spawning a part, fire a RemoteEvent from here and do the work in a server Script.

watchOut: Anchoring tool parts. Players freeze in place when they hold it. If a pickup must float, unanchor its parts in the `Equipped` event.
Having two parts named `Handle`. Roblox picks one at random, so the character might hold a sword by its blade.
Forgetting to weld multi-part tools. The pieces fall apart as soon as the player picks it up.
Expecting tool events to fire in a server Script for player input. They fire in LocalScripts, so send a RemoteEvent to the server.
